Vant

Agent memory that lives in your repo

Docs Brain MCP GitHub

Agent memory that lives in your repo.

Vant gives AI agents a brain: memory files the agent reads when it wakes and writes when it sleeps. Plain markdown in your own repository. Git history becomes the memory lineage.

Install Agent Onboarding GitHub 
# Install and start: layout check, health, ready
npm install -g vant
vant start

# Or serve the brain as tools to any MCP client
vant mcp
v0.8.6, open source, MIT

Three memory systems

Not one memory: three, with different jobs. All of them are files under models/ in your repository.

The brain

Markdown memory files: identity, goals, lessons, errors, preferences. Read at wake, written at sleep, inherited by every session after.

models/<scope>/<brain>/lessons.md
The brain →

The memory store

Key-value state and documents with TTL, written during the session. Sandbox-gated, atomic, per-brain scoped.

vant memory learn <key> <content>
Memory store →

Brain search

Semantic retrieval over the whole corpus. Pluggable embed providers, rerank for large corpora, git-backed citations for grounded answers.

vant search "why did the deploy fail"
Brain search →

Git is the feature

Your memory is files in your repo, so every Git workflow is a memory workflow.

Ownership

Your repo, your history, your backup story. Stop using Vant and the memory survives as files. Readable with cat, exportable forever.

Review

What your agent learned shows up in diffs. Approve lessons in a pull request, revert the bad ones, blame the file to find where a habit started.

Branches

One branch per agent. Each works in isolation, merges what is worth keeping. Experiments are branches, not forks of your data.

The agent loop

Written for agents first. The whole loop is three moves.

Wake

Check the layout, read the brain. One command tells you whether the memory is in the current multi-brain layout or a legacy import is pending.

vant migrate --status
vant start

Work

Write facts as they happen. Search the corpus when context is missing instead of guessing.

vant memory learn deploy-gotcha "Freeze deployments during migration."
vant search "migration rollback steps"

Sleep

Write the lesson, commit, push. The next session starts with everything.

git add models/ && git commit -m "agent: session learnings" && git push

The full agent loop →

Connect over MCP

Start the server and the module surface arrives as JSON-RPC tools: brain read and write, memory store, search, migration status. Auto-wired, no tool list to maintain.

vant mcp
# Discover tools from any client
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3457/call \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/list","id":1}'

Client config for MCP-native hosts:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "vant": { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:3457/call" }
  }
}

Runtime underneath

Memory is the product. The runtime makes it safe to run unattended.

Security chain

Sandbox capabilities, input validation, rate limiting, escrow approval. Every brain operation passes the chain; denials are coded, not silent.

Security →

Crash safety

A write-ahead journal and atomic writes. A crash mid-write leaves a recoverable journal, never torn memory.

Storage →

Multi-brain and crews

Named brain contexts with a stack. Branch-per-agent workflows. Trust levels decide how much each generation inherits.

Multi-agent →

Horcrux

A whole brain embedded in an image, encrypted. Cold backups, machine-to-machine transfer, restore anywhere.

Horcrux →

Any Git provider

GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted. Sync, rebase, and conflict detection work the same everywhere.

Integrations →

Headless and Docker

REST mode for CI and containers, official image on release tags. The brain outlives the container.

Server →

Think of it as a soul that reincarnates with full memories

That is the metaphor. On disk it is concrete: at wake the agent loads identity, goals, lessons, and errors from models/; at sleep it writes what it learned back and pushes. The next session inherits all of it, and git history keeps every generation auditable.

FAQ

What is a brain in Vant?

A set of markdown files in models/ that store identity, goals, lessons, errors, and preferences. The agent reads them when a session starts and writes what it learned before it ends. The next session inherits everything.

Learn more →
Where does the memory live?

In your own repository, as plain files. Vant never puts your memory in someone else's database. If you stop using Vant, the memory is still there, readable with cat.

Do I need GitHub?

A Git host is needed for sync, and any provider works: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or self-hosted. Without sync, Vant still runs fully on local files.

Learn more →
Is my brain private?

Yes. Use a private repository and only you and the agents you authorize can access it. There is no external service holding a copy.

How do agents connect?

Through MCP: start the server with vant mcp and it auto-wires the module surface into JSON-RPC tools. Agents can also use the CLI or read the brain files directly.

Learn more →
Can multiple agents share one install?

Yes. Each agent gets a branch and a named brain context. Branch-per-agent isolation with merge-by-PR keeps concurrent work safe.

Learn more →
What happens when I upgrade from an old single-brain layout?

vant start detects the old layout and imports it automatically into the multi-brain layout. Detection is content-based and idempotent, and nothing is lost.

Learn more →
Does Vant cost money?

No. Vant is open source under MIT. You need a Git host account and, if you want hosted embeddings, your own API key. The default hash provider needs nothing.

How is Vant different from a vector database?

A vector store keeps embeddings. Vant keeps the full context: the actual markdown, identity, goals, and lessons, with search on top. Agents inherit previous thoughts, not just similar ones.

Vant. Agent memory that lives in your repo. Open source under MIT.
